key_insight: NeFTY uses a continuous neural field as a differentiable 3D diffusivity representation coupled to a physics-aware forward model, enabling end-to-end gradient-based reconstruction of internal material properties from transient surface temperature measurements. This overcomes limitations of 1D pixel-wise thermography and fragile PINN formulations in transient diffusion settings.
problem_solved: Converts sparse, time-resolved surface thermography data into accurate quantitative 3D maps of thermal diffusivity by accounting for lateral heat diffusion and enabling stable inversion of transient diffusion PDEs.
method: Represent the 3D thermal diffusivity field as a continuous neural field (coordinate-to-property mapping) instead of per-pixel 1D models.
Couple the neural field with a differentiable transient heat-diffusion forward model so simulated surface temperatures are fully differentiable w.r.t. the neural parameters.
Perform end-to-end gradient-based inversion from measured transient surface temperature sequences to recover the underlying 3D material property distribution.
impact: Provides a practical, ML-native pipeline for quantitative non-destructive evaluation that leverages neural fields and differentiable physics — useful for researchers tackling PDE-constrained inverse problems, improved defect detection, and material characterization workflows.
visual_elements: Overview diagram: experimental setup (thermal camera measuring surface over time) → differentiable simulator → neural field → reconstructed 3D diffusivity volume.

paper_title: Neural Field Thermal Tomography: A Differentiable Physics Framework for Non-Destructive Evaluation
paper_authors: Tao Zhong, Yixun Hu, Dongzhe Zheng, Aditya Sood, Christine Allen-Blanchette
